shots.title: WHY AIRPLANE WINDOWS ARE ROUND
shots.purpose: Put the round window itself on trial before any history arrives
shots.claim: airplane windows are round by engineering necessity, not aesthetics
shots.evidence: full-bleed cabin window plate; the round shape is the subject
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in: stillness first so the question lands clean
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the archive-era aircraft when the history starts

subject_contract.expected_subject: round airplane passenger window seen from inside the cabin

one_second.relationship: the round window itself is the subject

shots.purpose: Land the contradiction: the proudest jet of its age broke apart twice
shots.claim: the world's first commercial jet airliner broke apart twice in flight in 1954
shots.evidence: early jet airliner plate + 1954 stamp under chapter chrome
shots.motion_reason: slow drift, then the year stamp does the informational work
shots.transition_reason: cut to the pressure diagram when narration explains corners

subject_contract.expected_subject: period technical reconstruction drawing of the de Havilland DH-106 Comet jet airliner, side profile, ink-line style
required: engines buried at the wing root

one_second.relationship: the first jet airliner, and the year it started falling

shots.purpose: One relationship, three stages: balloon cabin, corners gather, curves spread
shots.claim: cabin pressure gathers at sharp corners and spreads evenly around curves
shots.evidence: D1_stress stages: pressurized cabin, square corner stress peak, round rim even
shots.motion_reason: static hold; the staged diagram build is the motion (§13 INFORMATION_MOTION)
shots.transition_reason: cut to the cycle timeline when fatigue starts

one_second.relationship: corners gather stress, curves spread it

subject_contract.expected_subject: period technical reconstruction drawing of the de Havilland DH-106 Comet jet airliner, side profile, ink-line style
required: engines buried at the wing root

shots.purpose: The counter is the story: flexes accumulate until the hull bursts early
shots.claim: repeated pressurization cycles grow fatigue cracks until the hull fails far short of its design life
shots.evidence: D2_cycles stages: one flex per flight, counter climbing, 3,057 burst vs 10,000 design
shots.motion_reason: transformation: the crack and the counter grow together (§13)
shots.transition_reason: cut to the wreckage detail when the crack is found

one_second.relationship: thousands of flexes grow the crack far before design life

shots.purpose: Show the crack at cutout scale and pin the verified origin
shots.claim: the fatal crack began at a square-cornered antenna window cutout, not the passenger windows
shots.evidence: riveted skin macro with fatigue crack + origin chip
shots.motion_reason: slow push into the crack path
shots.transition_reason: cut to typography verdict when the fix lands

subject_contract.expected_subject: riveted aluminum aircraft fuselage skin with a fatigue crack from a cutout corner

one_second.relationship: the crack starts at the cutout corner

shots.evidence_justification: the typographic statement IS the explanatory visual (§6: large type can become the visual)
shots.purpose: The verdict in two words — geometry, not strength
shots.claim: the fix was geometry: rounding every pressurized opening
shots.motion_reason: type reveal is the motion (§13 TYPOGRAPHIC_MOTION)
shots.transition_reason: cut to the payoff window at altitude

one_second.relationship: the fix is geometry: round everything

shots.purpose: Loop back to the opening window, now carrying its history
shots.claim: the round window is a survival feature, inherited from 1954
shots.motion_reason: slow drift to rest — the strongest composition holds still (§17)

subject_contract.expected_subject: passenger view through a round airplane window at high-altitude dawn, wing beyond

one_second.relationship: the round window at altitude — still holding
